scope: Scheduled control cables and motor harnesses; not a complete cabinet power schematic.

groups.title: Motors & encoders
groups.description: All four drives: commands, motor phases, encoder feedback and DC branches.

groups.title: Drive alarms
groups.description: Four individual alarm cables plus the conditioned PB1 aggregate. Separate diagnostic views are included.

groups.title: Home switches
groups.description: Separate field and logic routes for X, Y-left, Z and Y-right.

groups.title: Coolant & air
groups.description: Flood and mist/air relay-control inputs. Pump and solenoid load wiring still needs its own design.

groups.title: E-stop monitor & buttons
groups.description: Safety-relay monitor, door, feed hold and cycle start. The energy-removal circuit is separate.

groups.title: Probe & tool setter
groups.description: Two independent sensor routes; actual harness and isolation-module pinouts remain to verify.

groups.title: Spindle control
groups.description: PWM, analog, enable and alarm references. Seven future supervision circuits stay reserved.

groups.title: Control power & USB
groups.description: Board supply, candidate isolated home supply and PC USB link. Branch protection remains to specify.

groups.title: Temperature sensor
groups.description: Reserved: sensor identity and its voltage, interface and pinout are not established.

groups.title: Old-drive rollback
groups.description: Four DM860T power records for preserving the old setup. Never substitute them for CL57T power wiring.

gaps.title: Oil / way lubrication, if fitted
gaps.detail: No oil-pump cable or dedicated lubrication I/O assignment was found in the current cable schedule and I/O manifest. Identify whether this is manual or powered lubrication, the pump model and voltage, and any pressure/level contacts before creating a route. This does not assign it to the mist output.

gaps.title: Pump, solenoid & spindle load power
gaps.status: Control routes are not load-power wiring
gaps.detail: FLOOD-CTL and MIST-CTL end at relay inputs. Supply-to-protection, relay/contactor load contacts, pump/solenoid terminals and spindle power/motor wiring need the actual equipment and a reviewed power circuit. No load ratings, wire sizes or fuse values are assigned here.

gaps.title: Mains, protective earth & hardware safety
gaps.status: BLOCKING HOLD before energizing: E-stop design is principles only
gaps.detail: The 56 records do not form a complete mains/PE, safety-relay/contactor or supply-distribution wire list, and the E-stop is specified only as principles. Before the cabinet is energized with any drive, spindle or coolant load connected, a qualified person must produce and review a stop design that removes 240 VAC spindle-servo energy (rated mains contactor on the servo supply and/or certified safe-torque-off; SON dropout is not the E-stop function), removes 36 V motion power with a Z-drop analysis for the de-energized state, puts the flood pump and mist/air solenoid supplies in the hardwired stop chain, sets stop category and restart prevention from a risk assessment, and gives a complete terminal schedule for the E-stop station, safety relay, contactors and the PF3 monitor contact. SAFE-MON only monitors the relay: its contact must be closed while the relay is energized, not an NC auxiliary.

gaps.title: Interface links & additional cable IDs
gaps.status: Some functional segments still have no scheduled harness ID
gaps.detail: Socket-to-interface and individual diagnostic links have functional views but no separate cable IDs. Interface/isolated-sensor supply feeds, conditioner-to-probe/setter GPIO links, internal alarm-aggregation links and FAN4-to-spindle-enable relay input also need explicit terminal schedules. These gaps remain visible; they are not silently counted as completed cables.
